title: Artemis Lunar Expedition — Blue Moon-style lunar-rendezvous training scenario
architectureStatus: Dated training interpretation of the public NASA October 2026 Artemis IV concept-of-operations updates. It is not a claim that NASA has selected Blue Origin for a specific landing.
publishedFacts: NASA's October 2026 update places Artemis III in Earth orbit in 2027 as a rendezvous/docking test with lander test articles.
NASA's Artemis IV page describes a crewed lunar landing in early 2028 at the lunar South Pole, with two crew descending while two remain with Orion.

The October 2026 Blue Origin concept uses transfer stages to deliver a Blue Moon Mark 2 lander to an elliptical polar lunar orbit, where it meets Orion; the lander then takes two crew to the surface and returns them to Orion.
The SpaceX concept for the same period meets Orion in Earth orbit and uses Starship to push the combined stack toward low lunar orbit.
NASA states that the lander provider assignment for the near-term landing missions remains to be determined.
Axiom Space's suit and two approximately two-hour moonwalks are part of the published initial surface-mission planning.
trainingAssumptions: This implementation selects the Blue Moon-style lunar-rendezvous architecture only. It does not implement the SpaceX Earth-orbit stack by default.
The lunar transfer uses a patched-conic training model with a 20,000 km arrival gate and Moon-only two-body motion inside the lunar sphere of influence.
The Moon follows a circular 384,400 km orbit inclined 5.145 degrees to the equator with a fixed training epoch phase.
SLS launch is a guided ascent profile with automatic staging and a physically validated 200 km parking orbit; it is not a 6-DOF SLS ascent simulation.
Orion, ICPS and lander masses, propellant loads, thrusts and Isp values are training values, not published flight constants.
The lander is a procedural Blue Moon-style proxy because no flight lander or usable interior was present in the repository.
The south-polar terrain is a procedural 2 km training patch; its height function is used for both rendering and collision. It is not LOLA data.
The EVA sample, photo and experiment tasks are training tasks; they are not confirmed Artemis IV flight procedures or instruments.
Voice communications remain the existing real-time social channel; the simulation does not impose a light-time delay on voice.
epoch: Training epoch T+0 at SLS launch; no real UTC epoch is claimed.
units: SI internally (m, s, kg, N, rad); HUD converts to km, m/s, kg and degrees.

limitations: No real JPL Horizons ephemeris or NAIF SPICE kernels are loaded.
No J2, solar gravity, lunar mascons or finite-burn optimization.
No exact SLS/Orion/Blue Moon flight model or certified entry guidance.
No Gateway, NRHO, HLS elevator, rover, or surface habitat; these are outside this scenario.
No real-time comms light-time delay or DSN scheduling.
The visual SLS/Orion asset is a derived copy of the existing display model; the lander/capsule/astronaut/terrain visuals are labelled proxies.
